result.title: Solving Go under Positional Superko: Sound Proof Transfer and New Board Values
result.summary: Positional superko (PSK) forbids recreating any earlier whole-board position. It is part of the Chinese rules as written and of the rules used in computer Go. Yet almost all solved Go boards were computed under a simpler basic-ko rule set. PSK makes solving hard: legality depends on the whole game history, and this breaks the three tools that make solving tractable, namely transposition tables (the graph-history interaction problem), static life-and-death recognition, and safe move pruning. We present Sanko, a parallel depth-first proof-number solver that restores all three soundly. Its core is a cheap proof-transfer theorem: a stored proof stays valid on a new path unless a board that the proof's winner must create has already occurred. Sanko proves 5x5 Go in 16 minutes with six threads, where the previous state of the art needed 5.25 hours with six processes, and in about a minute and a half on one 192-thread machine. It also establishes the first PSK values of twenty-three further boards, eleven of which were unsolved under any rules. Superko changes game-theoretic values: 4x7, a full-board win under basic ko, is worth only 12 points under PSK, and we pinpoint the move at which the previously published optimal line fails. Unlike earlier solutions of empty Go boards, we release the solver source together with the command line and outcome of every run behind our values and measurements, so that all reported values can be reproduced.

AI.brief_summary: 提出并行深度优先的 proof-number 求解器 Sanko，核心是一个廉价的证明转移定理，在位置超级劫（PSK）规则下重建置换表、静态死活识别与安全剪枝三种工具，并用它证明 5x5 围棋、给出 23 个新棋盘值。
AI.relevance_reason: 「缓存证明仅当胜方必须产生的棋盘未在历史中出现才依然有效」这一转移判据，可能与 latent 推理中跨路径复用状态、缓存有效性及停止/剪枝决策的核查有关，但该文为纯棋类求解，无视觉或多模态成分。
